title: The Dockerfile
description: A Dockerfile that starts from a minimal Python image, copies the package files, installs the package, and sets the entry point.

steps.description: This is the `Dockerfile`, created in the root of your project. The page says Docker is the right choice when your language has native dependencies or needs system packages. `FROM python:3.12-slim` starts from a minimal Python image, and `WORKDIR /app` sets the working directory inside the container.

These commented lines show where to install system dependencies. The example installs `flex`, `bison`, and `llvm-14`, and clears the apt lists. The page says to uncomment and modify this step for your project.

The two `COPY` lines bring in `pyproject.toml`, `README.md`, and the `mylang/` directory. The comment explains the order: copying `pyproject.toml` before the source lets Docker cache the pip install layer and skip it on rebuilds when only the source changes.
`RUN pip install --no-cache-dir .` installs the package inside the image.

`ENTRYPOINT ["mylang"]` is what runs when someone runs the image. The comments show the command `docker run --rm mylang:latest program.ml`, where the user passes the file path as the argument after the image name.
